source.title: On the Failure of Topic-Matched Contrast Baselines in Multi-Directional Refusal Abliteration

record.tranche_reason: The study tests refusal removal by weight-matrix projection using per-class SOM directions rather than the original single difference-in-means direction, and reports the behavioral effect.
record.gate_note: The paper reports direction-extraction comparisons, weight-edit refusal outcomes, KL divergence, capture measurements, and geometric measurements. The reported count of 859 prompt-category matches is a corpus diagnostic, not a behavioral or intervention outcome, so it is not a row.
record.test_reason: Applies abliteration-style weight edits on a released model (Qwen 3.5 2B) and reports refusal counts. It compares an unmatched harmless baseline with topic-matched baselines, so it bears on whether practical removal (V2) works and how it depends on baseline choice. It extracts seven to nine per-class SOM directions per layer, not the single difference-in-means direction, so it does not test V1 as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Topic-matched baselines give purer but inert directions (R stays 9–10). Unmatched bulk baselines give complete removal on six layers, with KL below 0.005 on three of them. The authors attribute the failure to topic cancellation shrinking direction magnitude, with SVD further diluting the signal. Results are limited to one hybrid model.
record.recipe_differences: Uses per-class SOM direction extraction, optionally followed by SVD orthogonalization, and weight-matrix projection; compares topic-matched against unmatched contrast rather than testing a single difference-in-means direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with contrast-baseline construction, SVD orthogonalization, layer, and abliteration weight. Topic-matched contrast without SVD gives a one-prompt reduction only at layer 9 for weights 0.8, 1.0, and 1.2; topic-matched SVD gives no reduction at tested weights. Unmatched contrast gives complete elimination at six layers, with reported minimum weights differing by layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Topic-matched harmful-minus-harmless differences have an order-of-magnitude smaller norm than unmatched ones, and their projection falls below natural activation variation. Directions with higher geometric purity were functionally inert.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Effective refusal-direction ablation depends on contrast-baseline construction; topic-matched baselines yield too-small directions for weight-edit removal.

record.problems: The behavioral evaluation uses 10 stratified harmful prompts. Results are from one model and the authors caution that generalization to dense architectures, larger scales, and other taxonomies is untested. General capability is assessed only through KL divergence on harmless reference prompts, not a direct capability benchmark. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

untested.parts: Single difference-in-means direction, inducing refusal by adding the direction, and direct capability benchmarks. Only KL on harmless prompts is reported.
Other released models and dense architectures; larger prompt sets. Only 10 harmful prompts are used.
Multiple directions are used but never compared against a single direction, so V4 is not tested.

missing.what: Synergy test of layer pairs at w=0.3: R=0 or R=1 in most pairs, and pair (14,15) gave +6 over the best single layer.
Canary false-refusal results are not reported, though canary prompts were included.
Claim that the first SVD vector at high weight is insufficient, stated without numbers.

record.verdict_notes: Single author, preprint, 10 evaluation prompts, no uncertainty reported. Qwen 3.5 2B is a hybrid linear-attention model. The text says the gap is 8.7 points in Section 4.4 but 9 points in the conclusions. The 859 category matches among 400 prompts suggests multi-label counting. The abliteration procedure is multi-directional SOM, so V1 rows were relinked to V2 only.

versions.untested_parts: It does not test the original single difference-in-means direction, adding the direction to induce refusals, or general capabilities directly; KL divergence on harmless prompts is reported as a proxy.
The weight edit is tested on Qwen 3.5 2B only; generalization to other released models is not tested.
The study uses multiple directions but does not test whether refusal is better described by an affine set, a cone, or a dominant direction plus others.

relation.reason: Reports its own refusal counts R before and after weight edits on Qwen 3.5 2B under three extraction baselines.

tranche.reason: Weight-edit abliteration with per-class multi-direction SOM extraction rather than a single diff-in-means direction, aimed at whether weight-edit removal works; the main finding is method-dependence, not a claim that V2 is wrong.

source_check.notes: The paper is a preprint by one author (INMECHA Inc), with no code. Each run uses only 10 harmful prompts, scored by the author's own three-tier classifier, and every layer is edited on its own. The paper contradicts itself: Sec 3.3 calls a configuration 'functional' if R<10, yet the abstract and conclusion say matched directions never reduce refusal, despite R=9 at layer 9. Table 3 (SVD) tests layers 9/14/15/23, not 11, so the S rows should use those layers.

statements.problem: Minor: M1 (w=0.3) is set against U1 (w=0.5), so the weights differ, but M2 (layer 9, w=0.5) is also R=10, so the contrast holds.
